newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris dismisses report wants Camdessus as ECB head.
newsitem.headline: Paris dismisses report wants Camdessus as ECB head.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac's office declined to confirm a German newspaper report on Tuesday that France had proposed French IMF managing director Michel Camdessus as head of the future European Central Bank (ECB).
But it restated France's position that who gets the post remains an open question.
At the finance ministry, a spokeswoman limited herself to saying of the report in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung:
"This is not an issue for the moment. France will make its stance clear when it is time to do so, in 1998 I believe."

Presidential spokeswoman Catherine Colonna would not comment beyond reiterating France's official position that the decision to make Dutch central bank governor Wim Duisenberg head of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner of the future ECB did not mean he would automatically become ECB head.

The German newspaper, citing unnamed sources in France and Germany, said Paris had put the Camdessus proposal to Bonn and that France had told Germany it would in return support a German candidate to replace Camdessus at the head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
It said France wanted a Frenchman to head the ECB as compensation for the bank itself being located in Frankfurt, Germany's financial capital.
Duisenberg is due to take the helm as head of the European Monetary Institute from current EMI head Alexandre Lamfalussy later this year.
France's official position was spelled out by Colonna at a European Union summit in Dublin on December 13 after the decision to name Duisenberg as EMI successor.
"The decision on the nomination does not prejudge the presidency of the European Central Bank," she said at the time.
